preamble:
I've reviewed `T-0001`. It's well researched, and criteria 4 and 5 are good examples of the board's rule that a criterion names the behavior it checks. My main concern is that it bundles two changes that get verified very differently. All citations are to pages under `/study/agentpatterns` that I read, including their "When this backfires" sections. I didn't edit anything.

Findings 1 and 3 change how the task is structured, so they're worth settling before you approve it. The rest are single-criterion edits.

findings.title: The task bundles two changes that should be split
findings.text:
**1. The task bundles two changes that should be split.**
- **The linter swap** (criteria 1–6 and 13) can be checked with commands. It could reach `done/` in one session.
- **The LSP plugin and its doc** (criteria 7–12) depend on an unfixed Claude Code bug (#72316) and on fresh interactive sessions. They also rest on plugin-loading details the Context itself says to "verify while implementing".
- **Why it matters:** if the LSP half stalls, a task only enters `done/` when every criterion has evidence, so the finished linter swap is stuck too. The blocked task also keeps holding the agent's single work-in-progress slot.
- **Suggestion:**
  - `T-0001`: the rumdl swap plus the ADR.
  - `T-0002`: the plugin plus the Handoff findings, with `depends_on: [T-0001]` since it needs rumdl pinned.
  - The `docs/tools/` doc goes with finding 3.
- **Source:** `verification/incremental-verification.md` says to put a checkpoint after each meaningful unit, and this is a clean one. Its backfire (units too small) doesn't apply here. `patterns/anti-patterns/assumption-propagation.md` warns about too many criteria (Kiro produced 16 for a bug fix). Splitting doesn't add criteria; it divides the 13 that exist.

findings.title: Criteria 9 and 10 can't be re-run by a different verifier as written
findings.text:
**2. Criteria 9 and 10 can't be re-run by a different verifier as written.**
- Each evidence entry needs a `command`, and `verified_by` must be a different agent. "In a new Claude Code session… returns headings" names no command.
- **Suggestion:** say how it's checked, for example a headless `claude -p` run in the main checkout and in a worktree, plus the `--debug` log line showing the server started. Or say plainly that this is manual evidence the user records.
- Criterion 10 ("records whether…") can't fail, so it's a research output, not a pass/fail check. It's worth keeping, but label it that way.
- **Source:** `patterns/anti-patterns/premature-completion.md` says to tie stopping criteria to observable state, not to a transcript saying it works. `verification/incremental-verification.md` makes the same point: "A checkpoint that reads the agent's self-report is not a checkpoint."

findings.title: Two agents own parts of one task
findings.text:
**3. Two agents own parts of one task.**
- The Context gives the `docs/tools/` doc to the coach, and ADRs are the coach's job ("records decisions the user makes"). But the task has one `claimed_by`, and the implementer and verifier must be different agents.
- **Suggestion:** make the doc its own coach-owned task that depends on the LSP task. The coach then works from that task's Handoff section, not from chat history.
- **Source:** `patterns/agent-design/persona-as-code.md`: when roles overlap on the same artifact, conflicts have "no principled resolution", and handing off files instead of chat keeps what was learned.

findings.title: Criterion 3 hard-codes rule values instead of the property it protects
findings.text:
**4. Criterion 3 hard-codes rule values instead of the property it protects.**
- What matters is that oxfmt and rumdl never disagree. The values listed (MD003 atx, MD004 dash, MD049 underscore, MD050 asterisk) are research findings about what oxfmt writes.
- **Suggestion:** add a behavioral criterion, and keep the value list or drop it. For example: a temporary file mixing heading, list, and emphasis styles, after `npm run format`, gives zero `npm run lint:md` issues. That catches a wrong value, or a change after an oxfmt upgrade, and a value list can't.
- **Source:** `patterns/anti-patterns/spec-complexity-displacement.md` says to put precision in things that enforce, like tests and linters, not prose. That page has no "When this backfires" section. `verification/deterministic-guardrails.md` covers the risk directly in its backfire item "the guardrail drifts from the property".

findings.title: CI isn't in the acceptance criteria, though the Context asks for it
findings.text:
**5. CI isn't in the acceptance criteria, though the Context asks for it.**
- The Context says to confirm the binary resolves "in CI", but criterion 13 only proves `npm run check` passes locally.
- rumdl gets its binary through platform-specific optional dependencies. The sandbox's `node_modules/` is a bind mount, while CI does a clean `npm ci`, so passing locally doesn't show CI passes.
- The sandbox is x86_64 like `ubuntu-latest`, which lowers the risk without removing it.
- **Suggestion:** add "the CI `check` workflow passes on the commit", or a clean `npm ci && npm run lint:md` in a fresh directory.
- **Source:** `verification/deterministic-guardrails.md`: CI is "a second layer independent of the local environment."

findings.title: Editing `.claude/settings.json` could turn off the gate's hooks, and no criterion protects them
findings.text:
**6. Editing `.claude/settings.json` could turn off the gate's hooks, and no criterion protects them.**
- That file holds the Stop/SubagentStop hooks that run `npm run check`. The Context says "add to it without disturbing them", but that's only a note.
- A malformed or overwritten file would quietly disable one layer of the gate, which `CLAUDE.md` lists as a Never.
- **Suggestion:** add a criterion that the four existing hook entries are unchanged, for example by diffing `.hooks` before and after.
- **Source:** `verification/deterministic-guardrails.md`: guardrails only work if they "always run".

findings.title: The doc's version-specific claims will go stale
findings.text:
**7. The doc's version-specific claims will go stale.**
- Criterion 11 already asks the doc to mark broken operations with the Claude Code version, which is good.
- **Suggestion:** also say when to recheck and delete that note, for example on a Claude Code upgrade or when #72316 is fixed. rumdl's own link checks (MD051/MD057) will catch broken links but not an outdated claim about a bug.
- **Source:** `patterns/anti-patterns/stale-ai-configuration-artifacts.md`. Its "pre-stabilization" backfire fits here: Claude Code's behavior is still changing, so keep that section short.

findings.title: Checked and not raised
findings.text:
- **Plugin supply-chain risk** (`patterns/anti-patterns/install-once-plugin-trust.md`): doesn't apply. The page's own conditions don't hold: local marketplaces have auto-update off by default, and plugin changes arrive as repo diffs.
- **Plugin runs code at session start** (`security/pre-trust-execution-surface.md`): its backfire case, a first-party repo you reopen often, is this repo. The existing hooks already run `node_modules/.bin/tsx`, so the plugin adds no new kind of risk.
- **Context length** (`context-engineering/discoverable-vs-nondiscoverable-context.md`): the long Context section is mostly findings an implementer couldn't get from the repo, like parity tests, the `rumdl fmt` damage, and the bug trace. That's what a task Context is for. Only small bits are discoverable, such as "settings.json already holds the hooks".
